summary: This bill extends Title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act authorities by amending the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 to change the sunset date from April 30, 2026, to June 12, 2026, with the change taking effect by April 29, 2026.

scores.thoughts: The bill is a narrow extension of FISA Title VII surveillance authorities by changing a sunset date from April 30, 2026 to June 12, 2026. It contains no appropriations, authorizations of spending, or budgetary provisions of any kind.
The bill text addresses only the extension of foreign intelligence surveillance authorities and makes no changes to tax law, rates, deductions, or revenue measures.
No provisions in the bill relate to healthcare delivery, insurance, public health programs, or medical regulation.
The legislation does not address firearms, background checks, or gun regulations.
No immigration, border security, or visa provisions appear in the bill.
The bill contains nothing related to reproductive rights or abortion access.
While FISA authorities support national security, the bill is solely a short-term date extension and does not authorize, increase, or decrease defense spending or military programs.
No environmental, energy, or climate-related provisions are present.
The bill does not address welfare programs, entitlements, or social services.
No education funding, policy, or school-related measures are included.
The legislation makes no changes to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
Although FISA can intersect with intelligence gathering, this bill is only a technical extension of an existing sunset and does not alter sentencing, policing, or criminal procedure.
No trade, tariffs, or international commerce provisions exist in the bill.
The bill has no fiscal impact and does not address deficits, debt ceiling, or debt reduction.
No provisions regarding LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights are present.
The bill does not authorize, modify, or eliminate any foreign assistance.
No election administration, voting access, or campaign finance measures are included.

FISA Title VII governs certain electronic surveillance authorities. However, the bill merely extends an existing sunset date by roughly six weeks without altering any substantive privacy protections, oversight mechanisms, or regulatory requirements. It therefore has no meaningful policy impact on the topic.
The bill contains no labor, employment, or union-related provisions.
No provisions address religious exemptions, civil rights, or anti-discrimination law.
